title: Sobolev realization and Rellich compactness for metric bundles
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its positive volume form $dV$, and let $B\to N$ be a smooth finite-rank real vector bundle with a smooth positive definite fibre metric. Define $L^2(B)$ as the completion of $\Gamma^\infty(B)$ for $\|u\|_0^2=\int_N|u|^2\,dV$. For an integer $s\geq1$, fix finitely many coordinate charts trivializing $B$ and a subordinate smooth partition of unity $(\chi_i)$ with compact support inside the charts. Define $H^s(B)$ as the completion for the norm whose square is the sum, over $i$ and multi-indices $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\leq s$, of $\|\partial^\alpha(\chi_i u)\|_{L^2(\mathbf R^m)}^2$, using the frame components and extending each localized section by zero. Different finite atlas, frame and partition choices give equivalent Sobolev norms and the same subspace of distributional sections. These are real Hilbert spaces; smooth sections are dense in each by the completion maps. The space $L^2(B)$ canonically identifies, with its integrated inner product, with measurable sections modulo almost-everywhere equality having finite $\int_N|u|^2\,dV$. The identity on smooth sections extends to a bounded injective linear map $j_s:H^s(B)\to L^2(B)$. Its image consists exactly of those $L^2$ sections whose localized distributional derivatives through order $s$ are in $L^2$. Here distributional sections mean local distributions in smooth frames with the usual change-of-frame rule. The induced map $L^2(B)\to\mathcal D'(B)$ is injective. The map $j_s$ is compact: every sequence bounded in $H^s(B)$ has a subsequence whose images converge in $L^2(B)$.

proof.text: For smooth sections use the integrated fibre pairing for order zero and the sum of the localized derivative pairings for order $s$. Both are positive definite: a nonzero smooth section is nonzero on a coordinate open set of positive volume, and some $\chi_i$ is nonzero at each point. The displayed norms are exactly their inner product norms. Extend each pairing to Cauchy sequences by $\langle[u_n],[v_n]\rangle=\lim_n\langle u_n,v_n\rangle$; Cauchy–Schwarz proves existence and independence of representatives, and the extended norm is the completion norm. Thus the two completions are real Hilbert spaces, with dense images of smooth sections.

proof.text: Put $K_i=\operatorname{supp}\chi_i$ and $f_i(u)=(\chi_i u)_i$, extended by zero. On each $K_i$, the smooth positive volume density and positive fibre-metric matrix have positive lower bounds and finite upper bounds. Consequently $c\|u\|_0\leq(\sum_i\|f_i(u)\|_2^2)^{1/2}\leq C\|u\|_0$; the first inequality follows by $u=\sum_i\chi_i u$ and the triangle inequality. These estimates also hold for measurable sections. Their square-integrable a.e. classes form a complete space: for a Cauchy sequence $u_n$, each $f_i(u_n)$ converges in Euclidean $L^2$ by the cited lemma, and the finite sum of these limits, put back into their frames, is the integrated-$L^2$ limit of $u_n$. For a measurable section $u$, apply that lemma with $s=0$ to each $f_i(u)$, choosing approximants supported in a fixed compact subset of its chart. Their finite sum is a smooth global section converging to $u$ in the integrated norm. The map sending a smooth Cauchy sequence to this measurable limit therefore identifies the order-zero completion isometrically with all such classes, including its integrated inner product.

proof.text: The order-zero estimate of step 2 gives $\|u\|_0\leq C\|u\|_s$ on smooth sections. Sending a Sobolev Cauchy sequence to its $L^2$ limit defines a bounded linear map $j_s$. Each $f_i(u_n)$ is Cauchy in the Euclidean $W^{s,2}$ graph norm and has limit $f_i(u)$ in $L^2$, where $u=j_s([u_n])$. The closed-graph assertion of the cited lemma says that its derivative limits are precisely the weak derivatives of $f_i(u)$. If $u=0$, that assertion makes every derivative limit zero, so $\|u_n\|_s\to0$. Thus $j_s$ is injective and its image has all the asserted localized weak derivatives.

source.place: Paragraph (3), nested analytic prerequisite in the existing blueprint.from.place; agent-written completion/weak-derivative details for Demailly VI §2 Sobolev setup and Rellich (2.2).

proof.text: Conversely let a measurable $L^2$ section $u$ have every $f_i(u)$ in $W^{s,2}$. The Euclidean smoothing lemma gives $a_{i,n}\to f_i(u)$ in $W^{s,2}$, with all $a_{i,n}$ supported in one compact $K'_i$ inside the $i$-th coordinate image. Reconstruct $u_n=\sum_i(a_{i,n})^{\mathrm{frame}}$, extending each summand by zero outside its chart. These are smooth sections. For each target chart $j$, apply the overlap bound with source support $\kappa_i^{-1}(K'_i)$ and target cutoff $\chi_j$ to each error $a_{i,n}-f_i(u)$. It gives $\|f_j(u_n-u)\|_{W^{s,2}}\leq\sum_i C_{ji}\|a_{i,n}-f_i(u)\|_{W^{s,2}}\to0$. There are finitely many charts, so $u_n$ is Sobolev Cauchy and its image is $u$. This proves the reverse image inclusion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), nested analytic prerequisite in the existing blueprint.from.place; agent-written completion/weak-derivative details for Demailly VI §2 Sobolev setup and Rellich (2.2).

proof.text: For a second atlas, frames and partition $(\psi_j)$ write $g_j(u)=(\psi_j u)_j=\sum_i(\psi_j(\chi_i u))_j$. The overlap bound with source support $K_i$ and target cutoff $\psi_j$ gives $\|g_j(u)\|_{W^{s,2}}\leq\sum_i C_{ji}\|f_i(u)\|_{W^{s,2}}$. Summing finitely many squares yields $\|u\|_{s,\psi}\leq C\|u\|_{s,\chi}$; swapping the choices gives the reverse inequality. The same bounds for weak sections and steps 3–4 identify both completions with the same measurable subspace. The overlap lemma also supplies the distributional coordinate and frame compatibility. A measurable $L^2$ section gives a distributional section by its locally integrable coefficients; local integrability and convergence against tests follow from Cauchy–Schwarz on compact supports and the Euclidean lemma. If this distribution is zero, every localized $f_i(u)$ is zero by that lemma's injectivity into distributions. Since $u=\sum_i\chi_i u$, the original a.e. class is zero. Thus the subspaces just identified agree inside $\mathcal D'(B)$ as claimed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), nested analytic prerequisite in the existing blueprint.from.place; agent-written completion/weak-derivative details for Demailly VI §2 Sobolev setup and Rellich (2.2).

proof.text: For a sequence $u_n$ bounded in $H^s(B)$ use step 3 to regard it as weak sections. Each $f_i(u_n)$ has support in the same compact $\kappa_i(K_i)$ and is bounded in $W^{1,2}$, since $s\geq1$. Apply the fixed-support Euclidean Rellich lemma successively to the finitely many indices $i$, retaining a subsequence at each index. The final subsequence has every $f_i(u_n)$ convergent in $L^2$. The order-zero estimate of step 2 applied to differences shows that $j_s(u_n)$ is Cauchy in $L^2(B)$ along it, hence converges there by completeness. This is exactly the stated compactness of $j_s$.
